steps.name: QC and library-size diagnostics
caveats: Do not drop sample_01 outright at this stage — this step only diagnoses; the exclusion decision and sensitivity comparison happen in the DE step
12000 x 13 CSV (first column gene symbol) — parse correctly to avoid treating the gene-symbol column as a sample
steps.question: What is the library-size distribution across the 12 skin samples (6 AD-lesional vs 6 control), and does sample_01's ~4x-below-median depth create an outlier in PCA/sample clustering that would compromise the DE model?
constraints: Use raw counts as provided; do not pre-filter counts before computing library sizes
acceptance_criteria: Reports per-sample total counts / library sizes and confirms sample_01 is the low-depth outlier described in the data profile
Produces PCA or sample-correlation plot on variance-stabilized counts labeled by condition and by sample, checked for whether sample_01 clusters with its condition group or is an outlier
Reports gene detection rate (genes with count>0) per sample, flagging sample_01 specifically
Outputs a QC decision note: whether sample_01 is retained (with normalization deemed sufficient) or flagged for a sensitivity exclusion in the DE step

steps.name: Differential expression: AD-lesional vs control (primary, all 12 samples)
caveats: n=6 per group is modest for NB dispersion estimation — report DESeq2 default shrinkage (apeglm-equivalent or normal shrinkage available in pydeseq2) log2FC alongside raw estimates
Filter out genes with zero counts across all samples before fitting to stabilize dispersion estimation
steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between 6 AD-lesional and 6 control skin samples using raw Salmon gene counts, modeled with pydeseq2's negative-binomial framework which normalizes for library size (including sample_01's low depth) via size factors?
constraints: Use raw integer counts as input to pydeseq2 — do not pre-normalize before fitting
acceptance_criteria: Fits pydeseq2 DESeqDataSet with condition (lesional vs control) as the sole factor on all 12 samples, using median-of-ratios size factors so sample_01's low depth is normalized rather than ignored
Applies independent filtering and reports log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) per gene
Reports counts of genes at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1, and exports a full results table
Produces an MA plot and volcano plot of the results

steps.name: Sensitivity DE excluding sample_01
caveats: This is a sensitivity check, not a replacement for the primary result — the primary DE (T2S1, all 12 samples) remains the reported result unless this step shows sample_01 is a clear outlier driving false calls
steps.question: Do the DE results (AD-lesional vs control) change materially when the shallow sample_01 is excluded (5 vs 6 comparison), indicating its low depth is distorting the primary DE call?
acceptance_criteria: Re-runs the identical pydeseq2 model with sample_01 removed (whichever condition group it belongs to drops to n=5)
Reports concordance between primary (T2S1) and sensitivity gene lists: correlation of log2FC estimates, overlap of significant gene sets (padj<0.05), and any genes gained/lost from significance
States explicitly whether sample_01's exclusion changes the conclusions materially or is a minor perturbation

steps.name: Hallmark pathway enrichment on DE results
caveats: Gene symbols in the counts file must match HGNC symbols used in the Hallmark GMT; report and drop any unmapped genes rather than silently failing
n=6 per group with GSEA pre-ranked is standard but underpowered for detecting subtle pathway shifts — state this explicitly
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between AD-lesional and control skin?
constraints: Use the locally staged human MSigDB Hallmark GMT (50 gene sets, HGNC symbols) as the gene-set reference; if absent at run time, report the gap rather than substituting a different collection
acceptance_criteria: Runs pre-ranked GSEA (ranking metric = DESeq2 test statistic or sign(log2FC)*-log10(pvalue)) from the primary DE results (T2S1) against the 50 human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets
Reports normalized enrichment score (NES), p-value, and FDR q-value per hallmark pathway
Lists significantly enriched pathways (FDR<0.25 per standard GSEA convention, or FDR<0.05 stated explicitly) ranked by NES, separately for up- and down-enriched in lesional vs control

Cross-references whether pathways implicated in known AD biology (e.g., immune/inflammatory, keratinocyte differentiation, lipid metabolism hallmarks) appear among significant results, reported as observation not assumed

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon-derived raw gene counts, 12000 genes x 13 samples/columns incl. gene symbol) with 6 atopic-dermatitis lesional vs 6 control skin samples, unpaired, single batch. sample_01 has library size ~4x below the median, so it is flagged for QC review and handled via DESeq2's built-in size-factor normalization (which already accounts for library depth) rather than being silently dropped; if diagnostics (PCA outlier position, dispersion behavior, or extreme size factor) show it is compromising the fit, a sensitivity DE run excluding it is produced for comparison. All scripting is Python only per user constraint, using pydeseq2 for count-based differential expression and gseapy/blitzgsea or a custom hypergeometric/GSEA implementation against the human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols) staged locally for pathway-level interpretation. Steps: (1) QC + library-size diagnostics, (2) DESeq2-equivalent DE analysis (pydeseq2) treated vs control with and without sample_01 sensitivity check, (3) hallmark pathway enrichment (GSEA pre-ranked) on the DE results, producing gene- and pathway-level answers to the research question.
